result.architecture_summary: The target architecture has a sound core: durable repository state, deterministic dependency calculation, one bounded worker per ticket, isolated Git work, bounded repair, and Unity/runtime evidence. The implemented system, however, is mostly a bootstrap planning and reconciliation platform. It can identify seven nominally ready tasks but cannot generically claim, execute, validate, merge, or complete one. Its canon and task-lifecycle models are also not ready for an iterative GDD: the RAG corpus is stale, tasks embed copied prose rather than stable versioned requirements, and live validation assumes every task belongs to the original bootstrap. Retain the small deterministic graph and evidence-driven execution principles; reorganize around thin gameplay vertical slices, explicit canon-change impact, a generic single-ticket runner, and automated Unity validation.
result.verdict_reason: The architecture is not fundamentally misguided, but two central claims are currently false: Tasks are not yet a genuinely living graph, and canon retrieval is not synchronized with evolving canon. Milestone ordering has also favored speculative correctness machinery over the first reusable gameplay execution path. This can be corrected without discarding everything, but proceeding with the broad proposed Milestone 2 would deepen the wrong investment.
strong_decisions: Keep durable state outside model context and derive dependency readiness deterministically.
Keep implementation completion subordinate to integrated repository evidence and merge state.
Use one bounded ticket and one worker before attempting parallel development.
Protect main with branches/worktrees and preserve failed branches and evidence for recovery.
Treat runtime Unity evidence as capable of overturning a static evaluator PASS.
Count no-op refinement as failed progress and bound every repair loop.
Separate repository-state facts from semantic LLM judgment.
Require humans to retain design, game-feel, scene-inspection, and merge authority.
structural_flaws: There is no end-to-end production path. taskcontrol only validates, lists, shows, graphs, and reports readiness; it cannot claim, dispatch, validate, complete, or recover a ticket.

The live graph is still bootstrap-shaped. Its validator requires all tasks to share the original reconciliation/verification provenance and requires IDs to form a contiguous 1..N range. Honest later additions, removals, supersession, and mixed provenance are unsupported.
The only task states are open and complete. There is no stale, needs-revalidation, superseded, blocked, or abandoned state for responding to design and implementation changes.

Canon synchronization is absent. The reusable RAG corpus predates numerous GDD revisions and is nevertheless labeled canonical; its passing tests validate the corpus against itself rather than against the current GDD.
Task records copy GDD prose and section labels instead of referencing stable, versioned requirement identities. Consequently, a GDD edit has no deterministic affected-task set.

The GDD mixes player-facing design canon with orchestration policy, agent ownership, token budgets, Git practices, and pipeline locks. This makes the design authority depend on the current automation architecture and encouraged verifier-driven edits to root canon.

Several nominally single-agent tasks bundle code, Input Actions, a central scene builder, serialized scene integration, future-owner interfaces, and validation that cannot be exercised until later consumers exist. Readiness therefore means dependency-ready, not proven safe to execute or complete.
The monolithic DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder and canonical scene are claimed by 13 tasks, creating a serial integration bottleneck and making future parallelism largely theoretical.
Pipeline/Reconciliation/outputs/current is stale after bootstrap and still says no persistent graph exists and human approval is pending, contradicting CURRENT_STATE and Tasks.
Test execution is not standardized: unittest discovery found zero TaskGraph tests because they are named smoke scripts, and one reconciliation smoke script currently fails.
observed_failure_solutions: Assignment 6 runtime-feedback ingestion directly solves the experienced camera failure where static evaluation passed an unusable camera twice.
The refinement progress guard directly solves the experienced no-op Refiner that reported success without changing Assets.
Repository scanning and the distinction among defined, builder-created, and serialized state address the experienced stale-scene problem after camera code changed.
Reconciliation against current main addresses the real risk of stale Assignment 5 goal-selection output being mistaken for implemented repository state.
The Assignment 4 critic/revision loop addressed observed wording drift, qualifiers lost during revision, and poor retrieval ranking for Frost Field.
Durable repository documentation and run outputs mitigate actual chat/context loss across development sessions.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: The 15-auditor multi-model reconciliation verification crew primarily protects against future large-roadmap semantic omissions; it has not demonstrated gameplay throughput benefit.

Progressive Decomposition and the Artifact Authority/Artifact GER stack protect against future missing-design invention, but the initial graph contains zero artifact tasks and no current gameplay slice needs the full platform.
GitHub Projects mirroring, leases, merge queues, parallel workers, and broad resource scheduling address later operational scale that does not yet exist.

Continuous backlog replenishment, daily token governance, automatic planning refresh, and full reconciliation deltas are reasonable future controls but premature before one generic ticket can execute.
Style-evaluator integration is speculative until there is a real authorized style-sensitive asset in the actionable frontier.
overengineering: Pipeline/Reconciliation contains roughly 11,500 lines of Python and the approved run contains 112 files/approximately 7.8 MB of audit state before a generic ready task can be executed.
From August 19 through the frozen commit, the reviewed HEAD contains 74 commits touching reconciliation/task-graph/pipeline documentation and zero commits touching Assets/NoSafeCircle.

The 15 parallel auditors, streaming field repairs, conflict arbitration, recovery installers, immutable snapshots, mutable current view, approval manifest, bootstrap marker, and persistent task copy form a large chain of duplicated representations.

Milestone 2 combines RAG refresh, scanner, cache, context builder, two decomposition modes, artifact proposal, authority gate, generation, multiple evaluators, promotion, and graph reinsertion. That is several milestones disguised as one.
Planning to mirror local definitions and dependencies into GitHub would add another state synchronization problem before local lifecycle mutation works.
Keeping old and newer GER implementations together and hard-coding Assignment 6 around one camera goal makes the apparent reuse larger than the reusable production surface.
missing_components: A canonical requirement manifest generated from the current GDD, with stable IDs, source hashes, version history, and change classification.
A canon-change impact operation that marks linked work and validations stale or needing reapproval without rewriting history.
Supported task lifecycle mutations and graph-delta application for additions, splits, supersession, dependency edits, completion, and reopening.
A generic adapter from a Tasks record to one bounded worker invocation; current Assignment 3/5/6 runners are assignment- and feature-specific.
A restartable single-ticket state machine with an append-only run journal and idempotent steps.
An available Unity execution lane that performs batch compilation, EditMode tests, PlayMode tests, and Windows build validation with machine-readable results.
Per-task validation profiles that distinguish checks possible now from deferred integration or playtest obligations.
A reliable completion transaction tying validation evidence, merged commit, task state, and newly-ready dependencies together.
Standard test discovery/CI for the Python pipeline itself.
A product-priority policy. The current ready list is ID-ordered and encodes safety only weakly, not player value or critical-path leverage.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary authorities are: human-approved game-design canon, integrated main for implementation truth, a small work ledger for intended work/dependencies, an execution journal for transient runs, and human approval for design/merge/game-feel decisions.

Reconciliation snapshots should remain diagnostic evidence, but the mutable current view, immutable run, approved candidate, graph delta, approval manifest, bootstrap marker, and copied Tasks records currently duplicate too much responsibility.

GDD design rules and pipeline operating policies should be separate. Agent ownership, token ceilings, locks, Git workflow, and retry rules belong in technical/process policy rather than root game canon.

Tasks should own scope, dependency, acceptance, and linked requirement versions. They should not independently assert implementation truth; completion should reference a merged commit and evidence manifest.
GitHub should be optional projection/visibility, not a second operational authority. Do not build synchronization until local lifecycle transitions are complete.
Run/lease state should live in one supervisor journal, not Tasks, GitHub, branches, and mutable reconciliation output simultaneously.
Approved design artifacts may become subordinate canon later, but a full artifact authority hierarchy is unnecessary until a real design gap blocks current work.
gdd_iteration_concerns: The project has already experienced rapid canon evolution: the GDD was changed repeatedly from August 19–21 after the RAG corpus was produced.
Today, a GDD change does not invalidate the stale RAG corpus, copied task evidence, context caches, completed tasks, or existing validation claims automatically.
The documented future response—hash detection followed by affected reconciliation—is only a proposal. No requirement-ID mapping, impact classifier, graph-delta applier, or revalidation state exists.

A full reconciliation snapshot is suitable for occasional audits, not ordinary synchronization. Treating every material edit as another global bootstrap-style verification will be too expensive and slow.

Required behavior: version canon, diff stable requirement IDs, classify each change as editorial/clarifying/behavioral/removal, and produce an affected-work report. Planned work becomes stale for behavioral changes; in-progress work pauses and rebases; completed behavior becomes needs_revalidation; removed work is superseded rather than deleted.

Historical plans and evidence should remain immutable, while the living work record explicitly records which canon version it currently satisfies. This distinguishes ongoing synchronization from one-time bootstrap correctness.
Human review remains necessary for semantic design changes, but the machine should present a small concrete impact set instead of requiring the human to reread the entire graph.
result.throughput_assessment: The current machinery offers modest planning leverage but no major near-term development leverage. It can save rediscovery of dependencies and identify a ready frontier, but every productive step after that is manual. Assignment 6 is hard-coded to a camera selection and evaluator rule; there is no generic task context, worker dispatch, Unity runner, or completion path. Meanwhile infrastructure work has materially displaced game work: 74 recent pipeline/task/reconciliation commits versus zero Assets commits, with only about 1,334 lines of Unity C# against a much larger Python orchestration estate. The likely near-term outcome of building broad Milestone 2 is more accurate planning about a largely unbuilt game, not development in days instead of weeks.
human_intervention_points: Choose the next player-visible slice and decide priority/cuts; the graph should not make product decisions autonomously.
Approve behavioral GDD changes and resolve conflicts between new canon and already-shipped behavior.
Decide architecture when a ticket discovers a cross-system contract or scene/prefab ownership change.
Inspect Unity scenes, prefabs, Input Actions, serialized references, packages, and build configuration.
Playtest movement feel, camera framing, encounter readability, spell balance, pacing, and art quality; automated tests cannot approve these.
Review escalations after bounded retries, runtime failures, scope growth, or no-progress attempts.
Approve or merge changes until automated Unity evidence and the one-ticket path have established a strong reliability record.
Authorize genuinely new design/content artifacts when a real missing-design blocker is encountered.

next_slice.title: Mouse-directed movement vertical slice with real Unity evidence
next_slice.why: This is the foundational player interaction and unlocks door selection and cursor-targeted spells. It also crosses the exact production boundaries the architecture must prove: current canon, Input Actions, runtime code, scene integration, tests, worker scope, and human game-feel review. Do not build broad RAG/scanner/decomposition infrastructure first.
deliverables: Narrow NSC-003 into an executable contract for click-to-destination, hold-to-steer, shared cursor-to-gameplay-plane projection, movement restriction, reset, and suspend behavior; remove duplicated criteria and distinguish immediately testable checks from later consumer integration.
Use the current GDD file and its SHA directly for this slice; do not use the stale 39-chunk RAG corpus.
Implement the behavior in PlayerMovement and the registered Input Actions asset, with builder/canonical-scene integration through the established Unity editor workflow.
Add automated Unity tests for click movement, live hold steering, pointer projection, restriction release, reset, and suspend while moving.
Run Unity compilation plus EditMode/PlayMode tests on a machine with Unity 6000.1.8f1 and retain machine-readable evidence.
Perform one human Play Mode pass for movement feel, pointer accuracy, camera interaction, and door-prototype compatibility.
Execute it through one bounded worker invocation or direct development; record what context was actually needed and only then generalize the smallest reusable task runner.
next_slice.proof_of_value: In the canonical scene, the wizard moves by click and hold using the project Input Actions layer, exposes one accurate shared world target, stops correctly under restriction/suspend/reset, passes automated Unity tests, and is judged usable in Play Mode. The run must demonstrate that a fresh process can resume from its task/evidence without rerunning global reconciliation.

do_not_build_yet: The broad Milestone 2 bundle as currently specified
Artifact Authority and Artifact GER framework
Another full-project reconciliation unless the GDD changes materially before the slice

alternative_architecture.description: Use a vertical-slice architecture. State: keep current GDD as human canon, add a small generated requirement manifest with stable IDs/hashes, keep a simplified work ledger with lifecycle and canon-version links, treat main as implementation truth, and keep transient execution in one append-only supervisor journal. Planning: a human selects the next player-visible slice; an LLM performs just-in-time decomposition only for that slice using current requirement records and targeted repository searches. Execution: a single restartable supervisor creates a branch/worktree and invokes one coding worker; a separate planner/implementer/validator crew is optional rather than mandatory. Validation: run cheap Git/static checks, then real Unity compile/EditMode/PlayMode/build checks, then a fresh semantic diff review, followed by human playtesting where feel or scene judgment matters. Recovery: journal every idempotent step, preserve branch/logs on failure, retry from structured evidence within a small budget, and block/escalate without corrupting task state. Unity integration: move gradually away from one monolithic scene builder toward feature-owned prefabs/configuration assets and small editor installers, with the canonical scene acting as composition rather than the write target of most tasks. On GDD change, diff stable requirements and mark only affected work stale or needing revalidation.
alternative_architecture.why_better: It preserves the strongest existing decisions while removing duplicated planning authority and making evolving canon a first-class lifecycle event. Most importantly, every infrastructure increment must close an observed gap in a real gameplay slice, so leverage is measured in playable, validated progress rather than audit completeness.

evidence.observation: The corpus declares document_id/revised_date 2026-07-30 and 39 chunks, while the canonical Markdown is revised 2026-08-21. No whole-document hash ties the corpus to current canon.

Tests assert fixed rankings, 39 chunks, uniqueness, and source-path existence; they do not compare chunk content or source hashes against the current GDD, so all 20 retrieval tests pass on stale canon.
Live validation requires IDs to be one contiguous range based on current task count and requires every task to have the same bootstrap provenance pair, obstructing honest post-bootstrap evolution.
Implemented commands are validate, list, show, ready, and graph. No lifecycle mutation, claim, execution, validation, or completion command exists.

The nominally single-agent movement ticket spans Input Actions, movement, pointer projection, restriction, reset, suspend, builder, and scene integration. It also contains duplicated suspend acceptance criteria and a validation requirement deferred until later consumers exist.
Thirteen tasks claim both DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs and the canonical scene, revealing a central integration bottleneck.
Documents two camera implementations that passed static evaluation but failed human Unity runtime testing, followed by a Refiner no-op and a fourth pass.
The runner loads Assignment 5's saved selected goal and a matching current_rule.json; camera-specific feedback language remains in the evaluator path, so it is not a generic Tasks executor.

The machine result is accepted_static and says human Unity testing is still required; the circuit breaker has consumed all three refinements. Final manual success exists only in narrative documentation.
The actual canonical player still uses direct Keyboard.current WASD polling, demonstrating that the core intended control scheme remains unimplemented.
No scenes are registered for build, confirming that production Unity/build integration remains incomplete.
The mutable current view still says Tasks were not mutated and approval is required before graph seeding, despite the completed bootstrap and 37 live task files.
The smoke test fails at the frozen commit because expected lowercase finding IDs do not match emitted uppercase R16 IDs.
There are 74 commits on HEAD affecting reconciliation, task graph, Tasks, or pipeline documentation and zero commits affecting Assets/NoSafeCircle during that period.
Git history shows repeated August 19-21 changes adding runtime ownership and pipeline constraints, proving that canon is already a moving target rather than a future hypothetical.

result.biggest_uncertainty: The repository does not record comparable elapsed time, token cost, or developer effort for pipeline work versus manual feature work, and the available Unity command-line capabilities on the developer's real machine are unknown.
